reviewBoundary: Four complete ten-gap fifteen-word original banks, two CET4-format and two CET6-format; ten distinct used words and five unused per passage. Same-author full-bank/context review only; no independent exam equivalence or calibration.

units.title: A movement made from still pictures
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: A movement made from still pictures
materials.text:
A small figure appears to walk across a table in a student film. Its apparent movement comes from a ____1____ of still photographs, each showing a slightly different position. Played in order, the images create the impression of continuous action.

If it moves between photographs, the background may seem to ____2____ even when the objects have stayed still. A stable camera makes it easier to see the intended change in the figure rather than an accidental change in viewpoint.

They take a photograph, move it a short ____3____ and take another. Large movements between frames produce a different effect from small ones. The spacing is therefore part of the film's ____4____, not merely an inconvenience during production.

A cloud passing the window can change the ____5____ of the whole scene. A desk lamp may give more consistent illumination, although its placement still has to be planned. 

After several minutes of work, they play the result. One unexpected shadow appears halfway through. Rather than ____6____ the whole project, they identify the affected frames and decide whether to repeat that section. 

The method is slow, but its slowness makes ordinary motion visible as a series of choices. A character's hesitation can be created by repeating a frame; a sudden jump can be made by changing position more ____7____. Even a very short film may require considerable ____8____. Planning does not remove the pleasure of discovery. It gives the makers enough ____9____ over the setup to recognise which surprises they want to keep. A few seconds on screen can then reward an afternoon spent looking ____10____ at small changes.

questions.explanation: Sequence is an ordered series of frames. Receipt/distance/control do not name the image collection.
Shake describes background jitter caused by camera movement. Whisper/abandon do not describe that visible effect.
Distance is the spatial amount moved. Style/brightness/patience are not lengths between positions.
Style describes the expressive character of movement. Brightness concerns light and receipt payment, not spacing aesthetics.
Brightness changes with illumination. Distance/control/patience do not name the scene’s light level.
Abandon means give up the whole project, contrasted with a local repair. Shake/whisper cannot take project in that sense.
Sharply describes an abrupt positional change creating a jump. Closely concerns attention and loosely low constraint, not the sudden shift.
Patience is needed for long work yielding a short film. Receipt/distance/style do not name perseverance.
Control over the setup makes surprises interpretable. Brightness/patience do not take this authority-over construction in the intended sense.
Closely means with careful attention. Sharply serves gap7 and loosely contradicts the precise observation described.

units.title: Why the ice cube changes shape
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: Why the ice cube changes shape
materials.text:
Water freezes into cubes and melts again in a warm room. These familiar changes involve the same ____1____ in different physical states, rather than the creation of a completely new material.

The shape of the tray determines the outline of the ice. Water does not retain that outline when poured into another ____2____. Calling something solid does not imply that its form can never change.

Melting requires energy. Heat passes from the warmer surroundings towards the colder ice, and the cube begins to ____3____. Warm and cold plates may give different results; comparison needs care. 

A crushed cube has more exposed surface than a compact piece of equal ____4____. That difference can affect the rate of heat exchange. Size, shape and contact with the surroundings all contribute to what is observed; room temperature alone does not describe every ____5____ of the process.

People sometimes add ice to a drink expecting an immediate, fixed result. In practice, cooling takes time, and the melting ice also adds water. The drink becomes more ____6____ as that water mixes with it. 

An insulated cup can slow heat exchange with the air, but it does not ____7____ the laws of melting. The question is how long cooling lasts under stated conditions.

The kitchen therefore provides many opportunities to ____8____ ordinary physical changes. A simple observation becomes more informative when it is linked to a clear question and a consistent ____9____. Yet explaining what happened can be more satisfying than treating the result as either obvious or ____10____.

questions.explanation: Substance names the same material, water, across states. Container is the vessel and mass amount, not material identity.
Container names a new vessel whose shape liquid takes. Method/aspect/applause cannot receive poured water.
Shrink describes the remaining cube becoming smaller during melting. Expand gives the opposite size trend; borrow/observe do not describe the cube’s change.
Mass is the amount kept equal when comparing crushed and compact ice. Aspect/method/substance do not specify that quantitative equality.
Aspect is a feature of a process. Container is a vessel, applause response and substance material, not a general process feature.
Diluted means less concentrated after added water. Concentrated is the opposite; mysterious concerns understanding, not mixture strength.
Abolish means eliminate, which insulation cannot do to physical laws. Borrow/expand do not express that supposed cancellation.
Observe means watch physical changes. Shrink/borrow/abolish do not describe attentive examination of them.
Method names a consistent procedure. Mass/container may be controls but do not name the whole observation procedure.
Mysterious contrasts the unexplained with the obvious. Financial/concentrated/diluted describe unrelated domains or mixture states.

units.title: Restoring the colour of an old film
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: Restoring the colour of an old film
materials.text:
Different surviving copies may preserve different colour traces. A restorer works with a set of ____1____ rather than an untouched view of the first screening.

One problem is separating damage from deliberate appearance. A dark scene may be poorly preserved, or it may have been designed to remain dark. Automatically increasing its ____2____ could reveal details while weakening the intended atmosphere. 

Production notes, photographs and contemporary accounts can provide useful ____3____, although each has limitations. A publicity photograph is not necessarily a reliable record of the projected image. 

Restoration therefore involves ____4____. Some choices are strongly supported; others remain provisional. Keeping a record of major interventions allows later workers to understand what was done and, where possible, reconsider it. A convincing result should not make the decision process ____5____.

There is also a distinction between repairing damage and updating taste. Removing every visible grain may produce a smooth image while ____6____ part of the medium's character. A restored film need not imitate the texture of a recent digital production in order to be watchable.

This does not require a return to every scratch in a damaged print. It calls for an account of which features are being treated as damage, which as part of the work, and why. Such explanations can ____7____ disagreement by making its basis clearer, even when they do not remove it.

The resulting version is best understood as a carefully reasoned ____8____, not an escape from history. New material or improved techniques may support a different treatment later. Preserving earlier versions and their records protects that future ____9____. Present access remains ____10____ by those materials and decisions.

questions.explanation: Remnants are surviving pieces/traces of earlier material. Unanimity/compass/illumination do not name the surviving set.
Illumination names brightness/light level being increased. Judgement/evidence/possibility do not describe the visual darkening contrast.
Evidence supports an inference about historical colour. Compass/unanimity do not name source information; interpretation is the conclusion, not the supporting material.
Judgement is the weighing of supported and provisional choices. Remnants are materials and illumination light, not the decision activity.
Invisible describes a process hidden by convincing output, which documentation should prevent. Edible and mediated do not express concealment.
Erasing means removing grain and its character. Celebrating would preserve/emphasise it, contrary to the loss warned of.
Clarify disagreement means expose what is disputed and why. Other verbs/participles do not take this explanatory role.
Interpretation is a reasoned treatment of available material. Evidence is support and possibility an opening, not the resulting version itself.
Possibility refers to future reconsideration. Unanimity would claim universal agreement, not the preserved option to revise.
Mediated means access occurs through materials and choices. Seasonally is an adverb and other entries do not express that intervening process.

units.title: The border around a species
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: The border around a species
materials.text:
Species may seem like natural boxes, but their boundaries can be difficult to draw. Biologists use several kinds of ____1____, including anatomy, reproductive relationships and genetic variation, and these do not always point towards exactly the same division.

Names allow researchers to communicate about organisms and connect observations across places and periods. But a name is more useful when its ____2____ is clear. Two studies may use the same familiar label while applying different criteria to decide which organisms belong under it.

Reproductive relationships offer one approach, yet they are not equally applicable to every organism or every historical case. Fossils cannot be observed breeding, and some organisms reproduce without the familiar pairing of individuals. A criterion that is ____3____ in one setting may therefore be less useful in another.

Genetic data add detail, but more detail does not automatically produce a unique boundary. Researchers must decide which differences matter and how they relate to the question being asked. A numerical threshold can make a procedure ____4____ without making the underlying choice free from debate.

Classification can also change when new material is examined. What appeared to be one widespread species may be divided; groups once named separately may be brought together. Such revision does not necessarily show that earlier work was ____5____. It may reflect improved evidence or a changed understanding of relationships.

For readers, the practical response is to attend to definitions and ____6____. What supports the grouping? These questions help distinguish an operational decision from a claim that every boundary in nature is perfectly ____7____.

A useful category need not be permanently ____8____ in order to support careful work. When categories are revised, researchers should preserve enough information to ____9____ old and new records. Otherwise, changed terminology may be mistaken for changed organisms. Clear naming serves inquiry best when it makes those distinctions ____10____.

questions.explanation: Evidence includes anatomy/reproduction/genetics used to classify. Methods are procedures, not the listed kinds of observed support.
Definition specifies membership conditions behind a name. Corridor/evidence do not themselves define how the label is used.
Practical means applicable/useful in a setting. Edible concerns consumption and fixed/sharp do not express feasibility of a criterion.
Repeatable means the numerical procedure can be applied consistently. Visible concerns seeing and careless inadequate care, not procedural reproducibility.
Careless is the negative judgement not necessarily justified by later revision. Temporary/fixed concern duration or stability, not due care.
Methods are procedures alongside definitions that readers should examine. Corridor is a place and other nouns do not collectively name the research approach.
Sharp describes a crisp category boundary. Edible/practical do not express exact separation in nature.
Fixed means unchanging, denied as necessary for usefulness. Temporary is the opposite and would not state the misconception being rejected.
Reconcile means bring old/new records into a compatible account. Dissolve means break down and other forms cannot express record alignment.
Visible means apparent to readers. Tactfully is an adverb; fixed/sharp do not express making conceptual distinctions evident as directly.
